newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks seen mixed to down, peso soft.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks seen mixed to down, peso soft.

text.p: Traders saw stocks opening mixed to down with market disappointment over recently posted corporate earnings and an expected slide on Wall Street stocks both weighing on local equity prices.
"We failed to react to the Dow Jones rally yesterday, but we will react on the downside. I still don't see much volume, however," one desk trader said.

Traders expected the recently weak peso to open softer and volatile under the impact of higher U.S. long bond yields in the wake of strong U.S. GDP figures. The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was up 14/32 to yield 7.02 percent in early trade.
Dealers predicted a wide trading range of 7.9400/7.9800 per dollar for the benchmark 48-hour peso. Pre-open bids stood at 7.9650/7.9750 per dollar, compared to Monday's close of 7.9380/7.9430.
Overnight rates on Cetes were seen opening up under pressure from a weak peso and higher U.S. long bond yields.
